prerequisites: Knowledge of Basque is assumed for this course.

learning_outcomes.text: Take awareness of the influence that higher education graduates have on the use and development of Basque, and rethink one's communicative role in that context.
Search, understand, synthesize, and critically analyze scientific information.
Agree upon, present, and argue for ways to address problems related to research, technical advising, teaching, and the professional world, leveraging teamwork.
Use consultation resources (especially those accessible online) to respond to needs that may arise in different communicative situations.
Properly create different types of documents used in university and professional environments (CVs, forms, protocols, applications).
Communicate on engineering topics considering the requirements of the communicative context: reports, scientific articles, popular science texts, lexicographical texts...

syllabus_topics: The text as a linguistic unit of communication: contextualization, structuring, and textualization. Text revision: adequacy and correctness.
Characterization of specialized communication. Oral and written texts.
Tools and consultation resources for text writing and revision.
Practice using consultation resources (dictionaries, terminological databases, corpora, and consultation centers).

Work on the basic principles of communication, and text production and revision, using textual genres necessary for communication with the members of the academic community: application forms, email, minutes, cover letter, CV...

Revitalization of minority languages and terminology. Term creation: resources for lexical creation. Terminological variation in developed languages and in languages in the process of standardization. Errors in term creation in Basque. Consultation resources: dictionaries and terminological databases vs corpora. Characterization of specialized registers: structure and orthography of compound words, use of referential adjectives, strategies for inserting symbolic resources into discourse, complex nominal phrases.

Work on the responsibility that higher graduates have in the knowledge, fixation, and creation of resources for the representation of specialized knowledge in Basque (terminology and phraseology), through critical analysis of consultation resources, creation of multilingual terminological lists, and production of encyclopedic and academic texts.

Pragmatic parameters and scientific-technical texts. Didactic texts and encyclopedic texts. Research texts and popular science texts. Most frequently used discursive operations and routines in specialized texts, and verb selection.

Work on the management of specialized information and the production of texts of different levels of specialization: summaries, scientific texts, bibliographic review... Also work on the communicative function of terminology.
teaching_methods: Lectures to explain basic criteria or resolve doubts
Autonomous student work to discover issues and seek solutions
Group work (e.g., to discuss solutions to different problems)
Individual work to develop personal skills and evaluate results
Monitoring by the professor in class
Use of computers to access consultation sources or linguistic resources

assessment_methods.method: Practical exercises (classroom practices, cases or problems)

assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation requires attendance at all sessions and timely submission of all tasks. To pass the course, it is necessary to pass all sections. Students have the right to be evaluated via a final exam, regardless of participation in continuous evaluation, by submitting a written waiver within nine weeks for a semester-long course. If the final exam weight is over 40%, non-attendance results in 'pending presentation'; if 40% or less, a waiver must be requested at least one month before the end of the teaching period. The extraordinary call consists of questions, tests, and exercises (50%) and a written essay on a defined topic (50%), and all sections must be passed to approve.
